supporting_observations.claim: At 13:37:54, Explorer wrote a UserAssist entry in Mia Santos's user hive whose ROT13-decoded path is C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe. This supports recent PowerShell execution, but the entry does not show the command or prove that a visible window appeared at the reported time.

The supplied process-creation records show a PowerShell launch at 13:45:23 under ken.ito, with the command to run the workstation patch script from FILE-BLU-01. A child wusa process then installed a Windows update. This later activity is consistent with the stated IT practice and patching schedule, but it does not establish what caused the reported window around 13:40.

known_telemetry_limitations: The UserAssist record identifies a PowerShell executable path but provides no command line, process ID, parent process, or execution output (T214-00084).

The supplied records do not show a PowerShell process-creation event near the reported 13:40 time; the recorded PowerShell process creation is at 13:45:23 (T214-00141, T214-00142). The available evidence does not establish whether process telemetry was complete.
claims_not_established: Whether the PowerShell activity represented by the UserAssist entry occurred at the exact reported time or produced the briefly visible window (T214-00084).
What command, script, or other content was run by the PowerShell activity associated with the alert (T214-00084).
Whether the 13:45:23 PowerShell patching activity was related to the earlier report; its recorded account and timing differ from the UserAssist observation (T214-00084, T214-00141, T214-00142).

unrelated_findings: GoogleDriveFS traffic to clients4.google.com was recorded from WS-MSANTOS-01 at 13:41:55 and 13:47:55. Google Drive is not among the approved file-sharing or cloud-storage services in the supplied inventory; track separately and do not use it to decide this alert (T214-00109, T214-00176).
